notes: Hierarchy: Scripture -> Chapter -> Module -> Lesson -> Verse.
Every Verse has one lessonId and no chapterId. Theme-owned verses are assigned to the first matching theme; overlapping references remain in question metadata.
Every module contains at most eight lessons, and every lesson has one to six verses.
Lessons are chapter-homogeneous to satisfy unique lessonId/verseNumber constraints; larger sections are split across additional modules.
Chapter numbers and source verse keys are retained as verseKey metadata; verseKey is an additive optional field for the supplied Prisma Verse model.
Question level, original question type, answer, options, hints, and references are preserved in QuizQuestion.metadata and QuizOption rows.
User and progress models are runtime application data and are not included in this content seed.

scriptures.title: Bhagavad Gita
scriptures.description: The Bhagavad Gita, organized as a structured Sanskrit learning course.

scriptureTranslations.title: Bhagavad Gita
scriptureTranslations.description: A thematic and verse-by-verse learning course.

chapters.title: Arjun Viṣhād Yog
chapters.description:
The first chapter of the Bhagavad Gita - "Arjuna Vishada Yoga" introduces the setup, the setting, the characters and the circumstances that led to the epic battle of Mahabharata, fought between the Pandavas and the Kauravas. It outlines the reasons that led to the revelation of the of Bhagavad Gita.
As both armies stand ready for the battle, the mighty warrior Arjuna, on observing the warriors on both sides becomes increasingly sad and depressed due to the fear of losing his relatives and friends and the consequent sins attributed to killing his own relatives. So, he surrenders to Lord Krishna, seeking a solution. Thus, follows the wisdom of the Bhagavad Gita.

chapters.title: Sānkhya Yog
chapters.description:
The second chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is "Sankhya Yoga". This is the most important chapter of the Bhagavad Gita as Lord Krishna condenses the teachings of the entire Gita in this chapter. This chapter is the essence of the entire Gita. 
"Sankhya Yoga" can be categorized into 4 main topics - 
1. Arjuna completely surrenders himself to Lord Krishna and accepts his position as a disciple and Krishna as his Guru. He requests Krishna to guide him on how to dismiss his sorrow.
2. Explanation of the main cause of all grief, which is ignorance of the true nature of Self.
3. Karma Yoga - the discipline of selfless action without being attached to its fruits.
4. Description of a Perfect Man - One whose mind is steady and one-pointed.

chapters.title: Karm Yog
chapters.description: The third chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is "Karma Yoga" or the "Path of Selfless Service". Here Lord Krishna emphasizes the importance of karma in life. He reveals that it is important for every human being to engage in some sort of activity in this material world. Further, he describes the kinds of actions that lead to bondage and the kinds that lead to liberation. Those persons who continue to perform their respective duties externally for the pleasure of the Supreme, without attachment to its rewards get liberation at the end.

chapters.title: Jñāna Karm Sanyās Yog
chapters.description: The fourth chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is "Jnana Karma Sanyasa Yoga". In this chapter, Krishna glorifies the Karma Yoga and imparts the Transcendental Knowledge (the knowledge of the soul and the Ultimate Truth) to Arjuna. He reveals the reason behind his appearance in this material world. He reveals that even though he is eternal, he reincarnates time after time to re-establish dharma and peace on this Earth. His births and activities are eternal and are never contaminated by material flaws. Those persons who know and understand this Truth engage in his devotion with full faith and eventually attain Him. They do not have to take birth in this world again.

chapters.title: Karm Sanyās Yog
chapters.description: The fifth chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is "Karma Sanyasa Yoga". In this chapter, Krishna compares the paths of renunciation in actions (Karma Sanyas) and actions with detachment (Karma Yoga) and explains that both are means to reach the same goal and we can choose either. A wise person should perform his/her worldly duties without attachment to the fruits of his/her actions and dedicate them to God. This way they remain unaffected by sin and eventually attain liberation.

chapters.title: Dhyān Yog
chapters.description: The sixth chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is "Dhyana Yoga". In this chapter, Krishna reveals the "Yoga of Meditation" and how to practise this Yoga. He discusses the role of action in preparing for Meditation, how performing duties in devotion purifies one's mind and heightens one's spiritual consciousness. He explains in detail the obstacles that one faces when trying to control their mind and the exact methods by which one can conquer their mind. He reveals how one can focus their mind on Paramatma and unite with the God.

chapters.title: Jñāna Vijñāna Yog
chapters.description: The seventh chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is "Gyaan Vigyana Yoga ". In this chapter, Krishna reveals that he is the Supreme Truth, the principal cause and the sustaining force of everything. He reveals his illusionary energy in this material world called Maya, which is very difficult to overcome but those who surrender their minds unto Him attain Him easily. He also describes the four types of people who surrender to Him in devotion and the four kinds that don't. Krishna confirms that He is the Ultimate Reality and those who realize this Truth reach the pinnacle of spiritual realization and unite with the Lord.

chapters.title: Akṣhar Brahma Yog
chapters.description: The eighth chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is "Akshara Brahma Yoga". In this chapter, Krishna reveals the importance of the last thought before death. If we can remember Krishna at the time of death, we will certainly attain him. Thus, it is very important to be in constant awareness of the Lord at all times, thinking of Him and chanting His names at all times. By perfectly absorbing their mind in Him through constant devotion, one can go beyond this material existence to Lord's Supreme abode.

chapters.title: Rāja Vidyā Yog
chapters.description: The ninth chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is "Raja Vidya Yoga". In this chapter, Krishna explains that He is Supreme and how this material existence is created, maintained and destroyed by His Yogmaya and all beings come and go under his supervision. He reveals the Role and the Importance of Bhakti (transcendental devotional service) towards our Spiritual Awakening. In such devotion, one must live for the God, offer everything that he possesses to Him and do everything for Him only. One who follows such devotion becomes free from the bonds of this material world and unites with the Lord.

chapters.title: Vibhūti Yog
chapters.description: The tenth chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is "Vibhooti Yoga". In this chapter, Krishna reveals Himself as the cause of all causes. He describes His various manifestations and opulences in order to increase Arjuna's Bhakti. Arjuna is fully convinced of Lord's paramount position and proclaims him to be the Supreme Personality. He prays to Krishna to describe more of His divine glories which are like nectar to hear.

chapters.title: Viśhwarūp Darśhan Yog
chapters.description: The eleventh chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is "Vishwaroopa Darshana Yoga". In this chapter, Arjuna requests Krishna to reveal His Universal Cosmic Form that encompasses all the universes, the entire existence. Arjuna is granted divine vision to be able to see the entirety of creation in the body of the Supreme Lord Krishna.

chapters.title: Bhakti Yog
chapters.description: The twelfth chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is "Bhakti Yoga". In this chapter, Krishna emphasizes the superiority of Bhakti Yoga (the path of devotion) over all other types of spiritual disciplines and reveals various aspects of devotion. He further explains that the devotees who perform pure devotional service to Him, with their consciousness, merged in Him and all their actions dedicated to Him, are quickly liberated from the cycle of life and death. He also describes the various qualities of the devotees who are very dear to Him.

chapters.title: Kṣhetra Kṣhetrajña Vibhāg Yog
chapters.description: The thirteenth chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is "Ksetra Ksetrajna Vibhaaga Yoga". The word "kshetra" means "the field", and the "kshetrajna" means "the knower of the field". We can think of our material body as the field and our immortal soul as the knower of the field. In this chapter, Krishna discriminates between the physical body and the immortal soul. He explains that the physical body is temporary and perishable whereas the soul is permanent and eternal. The physical body can be destroyed but the soul can never be destroyed. The chapter then describes God, who is the Supreme Soul. All the individual souls have originated from the Supreme Soul. One who clearly understands the difference between the body, the Soul and the Supreme Soul attains the realization of Brahman.

chapters.title: Guṇa Traya Vibhāg Yog
chapters.description: The fourteenth chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is "Gunatraya Vibhaga Yoga". In this chapter, Krishna reveals the three gunas (modes) of the material nature - goodness, passion and ignorance which everything in the material existence is influenced by. He further explains the essential characteristics of each of these modes, their cause and how they influence a living entity affected by them. He then reveals the various characteristics of the persons who have gone beyond these gunas. The chapter ends with Krishna reminding us of the power of pure devotion to God and how attachment to God can help us transcend these gunas.

chapters.title: Puruṣhottam Yog
chapters.description: The fifteenth chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is "Purushottama Yoga". In Sanskrit, Purusha means the "All-pervading God", and Purushottam means the timeless & transcendental aspect of God.        Krishna reveals that the purpose of this Transcendental knowledge of the God is to detach ourselves from the bondage of the material world and to understand Krishna as the Supreme Divine Personality, who is the eternal controller and sustainer of the world. One who understands this Ultimate Truth surrenders to Him and engages in His devotional service.

chapters.title: Daivāsura Sampad Vibhāg Yog
chapters.description: The sixteenth chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is "Daivasura Sampad Vibhaga Yoga". In this chapter, Krishna describes explicitly the two kinds of natures among human beings - divine and demoniac. Those who possess demonaic qualities associate themselves with the modes of passion and ignorance do not follow the regulations of the scriptures and embrace materialistic views. These people attain lower births and further material bondage. But people who possess divine qualities, follow the instructions of the scriptures, associate themselves with the mode of goodness and purify the mind through spiritual practices. This leads to the enhancement of divine qualities and they eventually attain spiritual realization.

chapters.title: Śhraddhā Traya Vibhāg Yog
chapters.description: The seventeenth chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is "Sraddhatraya Vibhaga Yoga". In this chapter, Krishna describes the three types of faith corresponding to the three modes of the material nature. Lord Krishna further reveals that it is the nature of faith that determines the quality of life and the character of living entities. Those who have faith in passion and ignorance perform actions that yield temporary, material results while those who have faith in goodness perform actions in accordance with scriptural instructions and hence their hearts get further purified.

chapters.title: Mokṣha Sanyās Yog
chapters.description: The eighteenth chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is "Moksha Sanyas Yoga". Arjuna requests the Lord to explain the difference between the two types of renunciations - sanyaas(renunciation of actions) and tyaag(renunciation of desires). Krishna explains that a sanyaasi is one who abandons family and society in order to practise spiritual discipline whereas a tyaagi is one who performs their duties without attachment to the rewards of their actions and dedicating them to the God. Krishna recommends the second kind of renunciation - tyaag. Krishna then gives a detailed analysis of the effects of the three modes of material nature. He declares that the highest path of spirituality is pure, unconditional loving service unto the Supreme Divine Personality, Krishna. If we always remember Him, keep chanting His name and dedicate all our actions unto Him, take refuge in Him and make Him our Supreme goal, then by His grace, we will surely overcome all obstacles and difficulties and be freed from this cycle of birth and death.

chapterTranslations.title: Arjuna's Dilemma
chapterTranslations.description: भगवद गीता का पहला अध्याय अर्जुन विशाद योग उन पात्रों और परिस्थितियों का परिचय कराता है जिनके कारण पांडवों और कौरवों के बीच महाभारत का महासंग्राम हुआ। यह अध्याय उन कारणों का वर्णन करता है जिनके कारण भगवद गीता का ईश्वरावेश हुआ। जब महाबली योद्धा अर्जुन दोनों पक्षों पर युद्ध के लिए तैयार खड़े योद्धाओं को देखते हैं तो वह अपने ही रिश्तेदारों एवं मित्रों को खोने के डर तथा फलस्वरूप पापों के कारण दुखी और उदास हो जाते हैं। इसलिए वह श्री कृष्ण को पूरी तरह से आत्मसमर्पण करते हैं। इस प्रकार, भगवद गीता के ज्ञान का प्रकाश होता है।

chapterTranslations.description:
The second chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is "Sankhya Yoga". This is the most important chapter of the Bhagavad Gita as Lord Krishna condenses the teachings of the entire Gita in this chapter. This chapter is the essence of the entire Gita.

chapterTranslations.title: Transcendental Knowledge
chapterTranslations.description: भगवद गीता का दूसरा अध्याय सांख्य योग है। यह अध्याय भगवद गीता का सबसे महत्वपूर्ण अध्याय है क्योंकि इसमें भगवान श्रीकृष्ण संपूर्ण गीता की शिक्षाओं को संघनित करते हैं। यह अध्याय पूरी गीता का सार है। सांख्य योग को 4 मुख्य विषयों में वर्गीकृत किया जा सकता है - १. अर्जुन ने पूरी तरह से भगवान कृष्ण को आत्मसमर्पण किया और उन्हें अपने गुरु के रूप में स्वीकार किया। २. सभी दु:खों के मुख्य कारणों की व्याख्या, जो स्व की वास्तविक प्रकृति की अज्ञानता है। ३. कर्मयोग - अपने कर्मों के फलों से जुड़े बिना नि:स्वार्थ क्रिया का अनुशासन। ४. एक परिपूर्ण मनुष्य का विवरण - जिसका मस्तिष्क स्थिर और एक-इशारा है।

chapterTranslations.title: Path of Selfless Service
chapterTranslations.description: भगवद गीता का तीसरा अध्याय कर्मयोग या निःस्वार्थ सेवा का मार्ग है। इस अध्याय में भगवान श्रीकृष्ण जीवन में कर्म के महत्व पर जोर देते हैं। वे बताते हैं कि इस भौतिक संसार में हर मनुष्य का किसी न किसी प्रकार की क्रिया में सम्मिलित होना अनिवार्य है। इसके अलावा, वह उन कार्यों के बारे में बताते हैं जो मनुष्य को बांधते हैं अथवा वे जो मनुष्य को मुक्ति दिलाते हैं। वे मनुष्य जो अपने कर्तव्यों को भगवन की ख़ुशी के लिए एवं बिना फल की अपेक्षा किये हुए निरंतर करते रहते हैं, वे अंत में मुक्ति प्राप्त करते हैं।

chapterTranslations.title: Path of Knowledge and the Disciplines of Action
chapterTranslations.description: भगवद गीता का चौथा अध्याय ज्ञानकर्मसंन्यासयोग योग है। इस अध्याय में श्रीकृष्ण कर्मयोग का गुणगान करते हैं अथवा अर्जुन को आत्मा एवं परम सत्य का बोध कराते हैं। वे भौतिक संसार में अपनी उपस्तिथि के पीछे कारण का वर्णन करते हैं। वे बताते हैं कि भले ही वह अनन्त हैं, फिर भी वह इस धरती पर धर्म और शांति को पुन: स्थापित करने के लिए समय समय पर जन्म लेते रहते हैं। उनके जन्म और क्रियाकलाप शाश्वत हैं और सामूहिक दोषों से कभी भी दूषित नहीं होते हैं। वे मनुष्य जो इस सत्य को जानते और समझते हैं, वे संपूर्ण श्रद्धा के साथ उनकी भक्ति करते हैं और अंततः उन्हें प्राप्त करते हैं। उनहे इस दुनिया में फिर से जन्म लेने की जरूरत नहीं है।

chapterTranslations.title: Path of Renunciation
chapterTranslations.description: भगवद गीता का पांचवा अध्याय कर्मसन्यासयोग योग है। इस अध्याय में श्रीकृष्ण ने कर्मयोग और कर्मसन्यासयोग कि तुलना करते हुआ यह बतलाया है कि यह दोनों मार्ग एक ही लक्ष्य तक पहुँचने के माध्यम हैं। इसलिए हम इनमें से किसी भी मार्ग का चुनाव कर सकते हैं। एक बुद्धिमान व्यक्ति को अपने कर्मों को भगवान को समर्पित करते हुए अथवा उनके फल कि चिंता करे बिना अपने सांसारिक कर्तव्यों का पालन करते रहना चाहिए। इस तरह वे पाप से अप्रभावित रहते हैं और अंततः मुक्ति प्राप्त करते हैं।

chapterTranslations.title: Path of Meditation
chapterTranslations.description: भगवद गीता का छठा अध्याय ध्यान योग है। इस अध्याय में कृष्ण बताते हैं कि हम किस प्रकार ध्यान योग का अभ्यास कर सकते हैं। वे ध्यान की तैयारी में कर्म की भूमिका पर चर्चा करते हैं अथवा बताते हैं कि किस प्रकार भक्ति में किया गए कर्म मनुष्ये के मन को शुद्ध करते हैं और उसकी आध्यात्मिक चेतना की वृद्धि में सहायता करते हैं। वे उन बाधाओं का विस्तारपूर्वक वर्णन करते हैं जो कि मनुष्य को अपने दिमाग को नियंत्रित करते समय झेलनी पड़ती हैं अथवा उन सटीक तरीकों का वर्णन करते हैं जिनसे एक मनुष्य अपने दिमाग को जीत सकता है। उन्होंने प्रकट किया की हम किस प्रकार परमात्मा पर अपना ध्यान केंद्रित करके भगवान के साथ एक हो सकते हैं।

Krishna confirms that He is the Ultimate Reality and those who realize this Truth reach the pinnacle of spiritual realization and unite with the Lord.

chapterTranslations.title: Self-Knowledge and Enlightenment
chapterTranslations.description: भगवद गीता का सातवा अध्याय ज्ञानविज्ञानयोग है। इस अध्याय में कृष्ण बताते हैं कि वह सर्वोच्च सत्य हैं एवं हर चीज़ के मुख्य कारण हैं। वे इस भौतिक संसार में अपनी भ्रामक ऊर्जा - योगमाया के बारे में बताते हैं अथवा प्रकट करते हैं कि इस ऊर्जा पर काबू पाना साधारण मनुष्य के लिए कितना कठिन है परन्तु जो मनुष्य अपने मन को परमात्मा में लीन कर लेते हैं वे इस माया को जीत लेते हैं और उन्हे आसानी से प्राप्त कर लेते हैं। वे उन चार प्रकार के लोगों का भी वर्णन करते हैं जो भक्ति में लीन होकर उनको आत्मसमर्पण करते हैं अथवा वे चार प्रकार जो नहीं करते। कृष्ण पुष्टि करते हैं कि वे ही परम सत्य हैं। जो लोग इस सत्य को समझ लेते हैं, वे आध्यात्मिक प्राप्ति के शिखर पर पहुंच जाते हैं और भगवान को प्राप्त कर लेते हैं।

chapterTranslations.title: Path of the Eternal God
chapterTranslations.description: The eighth chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is "Akshara Brahma Yoga". In this chapter, Krishna reveals the importance of the last thought before death. If we can remember Krishna at the time of death, we will certainly attain him. Thus, it is very important to be in constant awareness of the Lord at all times, thinking of Him and chanting His names at all times. By perfectly absorbing their mind in Him through constant devotion, one can go beyond this material existence to Lord's Supreme abode.

chapterTranslations.title: Path of the Eternal God
chapterTranslations.description: भगवद गीता का आठवां अध्याय अक्षरब्रह्मयोग है। इस अध्याय में, कृष्ण मृत्यु से पहले अंतिम विचार का महत्व बताते हैं। अगर हम मृत्यु के समय कृष्ण को याद कर लें तो हम निश्चित रूप से उन्हें प्राप्त करेंगे। इसलिए हर समय प्रभु के बारे में जागरूकता रखना, उनके बारे में सोचना और हर समय उनके नामों का जप करना बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है। अपने मन को पूरी तरह से कृष्ण की निरंतर भक्ति में समाहित करके हम इस भौतिक संसार से परे भगवान के सर्वोच्च निवास तक जा सकते हैं।

chapterTranslations.title: Yoga through the King of Sciences
chapterTranslations.description: The ninth chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is "Raja Vidya Yoga". In this chapter, Krishna explains that He is Supreme and how this material existence is created, maintained and destroyed by His Yogmaya and all beings come and go under his supervision. He reveals the Role and the Importance of Bhakti (transcendental devotional service) towards our Spiritual Awakening. In such devotion, one must live for the God, offer everything that he possesses to Him and do everything for Him only. One who follows such devotion becomes free from the bonds of this material world and unites with the Lord.

chapterTranslations.title: Yoga through the King of Sciences
chapterTranslations.description: भगवद गीता का नौवां अध्याय राजविद्याराजगुह्ययोग है। इस अध्याय में, कृष्ण समझाते हैं कि वह सर्वोच्च हैं और यह भौतिक संसार उनकी योगमाया द्वारा रचित और खंडित होता रहता है अथवा मनुष्य उनकी देखरेख में आते जाते रहते हैं। वे हमारी आध्यात्मिक जागरूकता के प्रति भक्ति की भूमिका और महत्व का वर्णन करते हैं। ऐसी भक्ति में मनुष्य को भगवन के लिए ही जीवित रहना चाहिए, अपना सर्वस्व भगवन को ही समर्पित करना चाहिए और सबकुछ भगवन के लिए ही करना चाहिए। जो इस प्रकार की भक्ति का अनुसरण करता है वह इस भौतिक संसार के बंधनों से मुक्त हो जाता है और भगवान के साथ एकजुट हो जाता है।

chapterTranslations.title: Yoga through Appreciating the Infinite Opulences of God
chapterTranslations.description: The tenth chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is "Vibhooti Yoga". In this chapter, Krishna reveals Himself as the cause of all causes. He describes His various manifestations and opulences in order to increase Arjuna's Bhakti. Arjuna is fully convinced of Lord's paramount position and proclaims him to be the Supreme Personality. He prays to Krishna to describe more of His divine glories which are like nectar to hear.

chapterTranslations.title: Yoga through Appreciating the Infinite Opulences of God
chapterTranslations.description: भगवद गीता का दसवां अध्याय विभूतियोग है। इस अध्याय में, कृष्ण स्वयं को सभी कारणों के कारण बताते हैं। अर्जुन की भक्ति को बढ़ाने के लिए वे अपने विभिन्न अवतारों और प्रतिष्ठानों का वर्णन करते हैं। अर्जुन पूरी तरह से भगवान के सर्वोच्च पद से आश्वस्त हैं और उन्हें सर्वोच्च व्यक्तित्व के रूप में घोषित करते हैं। वे कृष्ण से प्रार्थना करते हैं कि वे अपनी अन्य दिव्य महिमाओं के बारेमे बताएं जो कि सुनने में अमृत सामान हैं।

chapterTranslations.title: Yoga through Beholding the Cosmic Form of God
chapterTranslations.description: The eleventh chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is "Vishwaroopa Darshana Yoga". In this chapter, Arjuna requests Krishna to reveal His Universal Cosmic Form that encompasses all the universes, the entire existence. Arjuna is granted divine vision to be able to see the entirety of creation in the body of the Supreme Lord Krishna.

chapterTranslations.title: Yoga through Beholding the Cosmic Form of God
chapterTranslations.description: भगवद गीता का ग्यारहवा अध्याय विश्वरूपदर्शनयोग है। इस अध्याय में, अर्जुन कृष्ण को अपने विश्व रूप को प्रकट करने का अनुरोध करते हैं जो की सारे विश्वों अथवा संपूर्ण अस्तित्व का स्त्रोत है। भगवान कृष्ण के शरीर में पूरी सृष्टि को देखने में सक्षम होने के लिए अर्जुन को दिव्य दृष्टि दी जाती है।

chapterTranslations.title: The Yoga of Devotion
chapterTranslations.description: The twelfth chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is "Bhakti Yoga". In this chapter, Krishna emphasizes the superiority of Bhakti Yoga (the path of devotion) over all other types of spiritual disciplines and reveals various aspects of devotion. He further explains that the devotees who perform pure devotional service to Him, with their consciousness, merged in Him and all their actions dedicated to Him, are quickly liberated from the cycle of life and death. He also describes the various qualities of the devotees who are very dear to Him.

chapterTranslations.title: The Yoga of Devotion
chapterTranslations.description: भगवद गीता का बारहवां अध्याय भक्तियोग है। इस अध्याय में, कृष्ण भक्ति योग की श्रेष्ठता पर बल देते हैं और भक्ति के विभिन्न पहलुओं का वर्णन करते हैं। वे आगे बताते हैं कि वे भक्त जो अपने सभी कर्म उनको समर्पित करके, अपनी चेतना उनमें विलीन करके, सच्चे मन से उनकी भक्ति करते हैं वे बहुत जल्दी जीवन और मृत्यु के चक्र से मुक्ति पा लेते हैं। वे अपने सबसे प्रिय भक्तों के विभिन्न गुड़ों का भी वर्णन करते हैं।

chapterTranslations.title: Yoga through Distinguishing the Field and the Knower of the Field
chapterTranslations.description: The thirteenth chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is "Ksetra Ksetrajna Vibhaaga Yoga". The word "kshetra" means "the field", and the "kshetrajna" means "the knower of the field". We can think of our material body as the field and our immortal soul as the knower of the field. In this chapter, Krishna discriminates between the physical body and the immortal soul. He explains that the physical body is temporary and perishable whereas the soul is permanent and eternal. The physical body can be destroyed but the soul can never be destroyed. The chapter then describes God, who is the Supreme Soul. All the individual souls have originated from the Supreme Soul. One who clearly understands the difference between the body, the Soul and the Supreme Soul attains the realization of Brahman.

chapterTranslations.title: Yoga through Distinguishing the Field and the Knower of the Field
chapterTranslations.description: भगवद गीता का तेरवाह अध्याय क्षेत्र-क्षेत्रज्ञविभागयोग है। क्षेत्र शब्द का मतलब भूमि और क्षेत्ररक्षण का मतलब क्षेत्र का जानकार है। हमारा भौतिक शरीर क्षेत्र के सामान है और हमारी अमर आत्मा क्षेत्र के जानकार के सामान है। इस अध्याय में, कृष्ण भौतिक शरीर और अमर आत्मा के बीच भेद करते हैं। वह बताते हैं कि भौतिक शरीर अस्थायी और विनाशकारी है जबकि आत्मा स्थायी और शाश्वत है। भौतिक शरीर नष्ट हो सकता है लेकिन आत्मा कभी भी नष्ट नहीं हो सकती। यह अध्याय फिर भगवान का वर्णन करता है, जो की सर्वोच्च आत्मा हैं। सभी व्यक्तिगत आत्माएं सर्वोच्च आत्मा से उत्पन्न हुई हैं। जो स्पष्ट रूप से शरीर, आत्मा और सर्वोच्च आत्मा के बीच अंतर को समझ लेता है वह परमात्मा को प्राप्त कर लेता है।

chapterTranslations.title: Yoga through Understanding the Three Modes of Material Nature
chapterTranslations.description: The fourteenth chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is "Gunatraya Vibhaga Yoga". In this chapter, Krishna reveals the three gunas (modes) of the material nature - goodness, passion and ignorance which everything in the material existence is influenced by. He further explains the essential characteristics of each of these modes, their cause and how they influence a living entity affected by them. He then reveals the various characteristics of the persons who have gone beyond these gunas. The chapter ends with Krishna reminding us of the power of pure devotion to God and how attachment to God can help us transcend these gunas.

chapterTranslations.title: Yoga through Understanding the Three Modes of Material Nature
chapterTranslations.description: भगवद गीता का चौदहवा अध्याय गुणत्रयविभागयोग है। इस अध्याय में, कृष्ण भौतिक प्रकृति के तीन गुणों का वर्णन करते हैं जिनसे भौतिक संसार में सब कुछ प्रभावित होता है - अच्छाई, लालसा और अज्ञान। आगे वह इन तीनों गुणों के प्रधान अभिलक्षणों अथवा कारणों का वर्णन करते हैं और बताते हैं कि कैसे ये तीनों गुण मनुष्य को प्रभावित करते हैं। फिर वह ऐसे व्यक्तियों की विभिन्न विशेषताओं का वर्णन करते हैं जो कि इन गुणों पर जीत पा चुके हैं। इस अध्याय के अंत में कृष्ण हमें सच्ची भक्ति कि शक्ति का स्मरण कराते हैं और बताते हैं की हम कैसे भगवन के साथ जुड़ कर इन गुणों को पार कर सकते हैं।

chapterTranslations.title: The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Personality
chapterTranslations.description: The fifteenth chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is "Purushottama Yoga". In Sanskrit, Purusha means the "All-pervading God", and Purushottam means the timeless & transcendental aspect of God.        Krishna reveals that the purpose of this Transcendental knowledge of the God is to detach ourselves from the bondage of the material world and to understand Krishna as the Supreme Divine Personality, who is the eternal controller and sustainer of the world. One who understands this Ultimate Truth surrenders to Him and engages in His devotional service.

chapterTranslations.title: The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Personality
chapterTranslations.description: भगवद गीता का पंद्रहवा अध्याय पुरुषोत्तमयोग है। संस्कृत में, पुरूष का मतलब सर्वव्यापी भगवान है, और पुरुषोत्तम का मतलब है ईश्वर का कालातीत और पारस्परिक पहलू। कृष्णा बताते हैं कि ईश्वर के इस महान ज्ञान का उद्देश्य भौतिक संसार के बंधन से खुद को अलग करना है और कृष्ण को सर्वोच्च दिव्य व्यक्तित्व के रूप में समझना है, जो विश्व के शाश्वत नियंत्रक और निर्वाहक हैं। जो इस परम सत्य को समझता है वह प्रभु को समर्पण करता है और उनकी भक्ति सेवा में संलग्न हो जाता है।

chapterTranslations.title: Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures
chapterTranslations.description: The sixteenth chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is "Daivasura Sampad Vibhaga Yoga". In this chapter, Krishna describes explicitly the two kinds of natures among human beings - divine and demoniac. Those who possess demonaic qualities associate themselves with the modes of passion and ignorance do not follow the regulations of the scriptures and embrace materialistic views. These people attain lower births and further material bondage. But people who possess divine qualities, follow the instructions of the scriptures, associate themselves with the mode of goodness and purify the mind through spiritual practices. This leads to the enhancement of divine qualities and they eventually attain spiritual realization.

chapterTranslations.title: Yoga through Discerning the Divine and Demoniac Natures
chapterTranslations.description: भगवद गीता का सोलहवा अध्याय दैवासुरसम्पद्विभागयोग है। इस अध्याय में, कृष्ण स्पष्ट रूप से मानवों की दो प्रकार की प्रकृतियों का वर्णन करते हैं- दैवीय और दानवीय। दानवीय स्वभाव वाले लोग स्वयं को लालसा और अज्ञान के तरीकों से जोड़ते हैं, शास्त्रों के नियमों का पालन नहीं करते हैं और भौतिक विचारों को ग्रहण करते हैं। ये लोग निचली जातियों में जन्म लेते हैं और भौतिक बंधनों में और भी बंध जाते हैं। परन्तु जो लोग दैवीय स्वभाव वाले होते हैं, वे शास्त्रों के निर्देशों का पालन करते हैं, अच्छे काम करते हैं और आध्यात्मिक प्रथाओं के माध्यम से मन को शुद्ध करते हैं। इससे दैवीय गुणों में वृद्धि होती है और वे अंततः आध्यात्मिक प्राप्ति प्राप्त करते हैं।

chapterTranslations.title: Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith
chapterTranslations.description: The seventeenth chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is "Sraddhatraya Vibhaga Yoga". In this chapter, Krishna describes the three types of faith corresponding to the three modes of the material nature. Lord Krishna further reveals that it is the nature of faith that determines the quality of life and the character of living entities. Those who have faith in passion and ignorance perform actions that yield temporary, material results while those who have faith in goodness perform actions in accordance with scriptural instructions and hence their hearts get further purified.

chapterTranslations.title: Yoga through Discerning the Three Divisions of Faith
chapterTranslations.description: भगवद गीता का सत्रहवा अध्याय श्रद्धात्रयविभागयोग है। इस अध्याय में, कृष्ण भौतिक प्रकृति के तीन गुणों से संबंधित तीन प्रकार के विश्वासों का वर्णन करते हैं। भगवान कृष्ण आगे बताते हैं कि यह विश्वास की प्रकृति है जो जीवन की गुणवत्ता और जीवित संस्थाओं के चरित्र को निर्धारित करती है। जो लोग लालसा और अज्ञानता में विश्वास रखते हैं, वे ऐसे कार्य करते हैं जो कि अस्थायी और भौतिक फल देते हैं परन्तु जो लोग अच्छाई में विश्वास रखते हैं वे शास्त्रपूर्ण निर्देशों के अनुसार कार्य करते हैं और इसलिए उन्हें स्थायी और अधिक प्रवीण फल प्राप्त होते हैं जो मन को और भी शुद्ध करते हैं।

chapterTranslations.title: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
chapterTranslations.description: The eighteenth chapter of the Bhagavad Gita is "Moksha Sanyas Yoga". Arjuna requests the Lord to explain the difference between the two types of renunciations - sanyaas(renunciation of actions) and tyaag(renunciation of desires). Krishna explains that a sanyaasi is one who abandons family and society in order to practise spiritual discipline whereas a tyaagi is one who performs their duties without attachment to the rewards of their actions and dedicating them to the God. Krishna recommends the second kind of renunciation - tyaag. Krishna then gives a detailed analysis of the effects of the three modes of material nature. He declares that the highest path of spirituality is pure, unconditional loving service unto the Supreme Divine Personality, Krishna. If we always remember Him, keep chanting His name and dedicate all our actions unto Him, take refuge in Him and make Him our Supreme goal, then by His grace, we will surely overcome all obstacles and difficulties and be freed from this cycle of birth and death.

chapterTranslations.title: Yoga through the Perfection of Renunciation and Surrender
chapterTranslations.description: भगवद गीता का अठारहवा अध्याय मोक्षसन्यासयोग है। अर्जुन कृष्ण से अनुरोध करते हैं कि वे संन्यास और त्याग के बीच अंतर को समझाने की कृपा करें। कृष्ण बताते हैं कि एक संन्यासी वह है जो आध्यात्मिक अनुशासन का अभ्यास करने के लिए परिवार और समाज को त्याग देता है जबकि एक त्यागी वह है जो अपने कर्मों के फलों कि चिंता करे बिना भगवन को समर्पित करके कर्म करता रहता है। कृष्ण बताते हैं कि त्याग संन्यास से श्रेष्ठ है। फिर कृष्णा भौतिक संसार के तीन प्रकार के गुणों का विस्तारपूर्वक वर्णन करते हैं। कृष्णा घोषणा करते हैं कि परमात्मा की शुद्ध एवं सत्य भक्ति ही आध्यात्मिकता का उच्चतम मार्ग है। अगर हम हर क्षण उनका स्मरण करते रहें, उनका नाम जपते रहें, अपना सर्वस्व उनको समर्पित कर दें, उन्हें ही अपना सर्वोच्च लक्ष्य बना लें तो उनकी कृपा से हम निश्चित रूप से सभी बाधाओं और कठिनाइओं को दूर कर पाएंगे और इस जन्म और मृत्यु के चक्र से मुक्त हो पाएंगे।

modules.description: Meet Arjuna on the battlefield as concern for family, duty, and the consequences of violence overwhelm him. Notice how admitting confusion opens the way to learning.

modules.title: The Eternal Soul
modules.description: Explore Krishna's teaching that the embodied self is distinct from the changing body, and consider how this view reframes loss and change.

modules.title: Act Without Attachment
modules.description: Learn the Gita's influential teaching on action: attend to the work you can do without making its reward the sole measure of your choices.

modules.title: The Steady Mind
modules.description: Meet the sthitaprajna, the person of steady wisdom, and examine the Gita's account of desire, attention, and inner balance.

modules.title: Duty and Selfless Service
modules.description: See why action is unavoidable and how work performed with care and without selfish attachment can support a wider good.

modules.title: Knowledge and Renewal
modules.description: Explore the transmission of yoga, Krishna's account of restoring dharma, and the role of knowledge in freeing action from confusion.

modules.title: Training the Mind
modules.description: Learn the Gita's practical response to a restless mind: repeated practice, detachment, and patient redirection.

modules.title: Devotion in Daily Life
modules.description: Study devotion as remembrance, offering, and a way of meeting ordinary actions with sincerity and care.

modules.title: Seeing the Divine
modules.description: Follow Arjuna's request to see Krishna's universal form and reflect on how the Gita presents the divine presence throughout existence.

modules.title: Choice and Surrender
modules.description: Reach the dialogue's close: Krishna offers instruction, Arjuna reflects, and the learner is invited to act with understanding and resolve.

lessonContentBlocks.title: A crisis becomes a question — Lesson 1

• Distinguish grief from a considered resolution

verses.sanskrit:
धृतराष्ट्र उवाच

धर्मक्षेत्रे कुरुक्षेत्रे समवेता युयुत्सवः।

मामकाः पाण्डवाश्चैव किमकुर्वत सञ्जय।।1.1।।
verses.transliteration:
dhṛitarāśhtra uvācha
dharma-kṣhetre kuru-kṣhetre samavetā yuyutsavaḥ
māmakāḥ pāṇḍavāśhchaiva kimakurvata sañjaya

translations.content: The King Dhritarashtra asked, "O Sanjaya! What happened on the sacred battlefield of Kurukshetra when my people and the Pandavas gathered?"

others.Commentary There are severla paths to reach the knowledge of the Self according to the nature or temperament and capacity of the individual. The first path is the Yoga of meditation taught by Maharshi Patanjali. The Raja Yogins behold the Supreme Self in the self (Buddhi) by the self (purified mind). Meditation is a continous and unbroken flow of thought of the Self like the flow of oil from one vessel to another. Through concentration hearing and the other senses are withdrawn into the mind. The senses are not allowed to run towards their respective sensual objects. They are kept under proper check and control through the process of abstraction. Then the mind itself is made to abide in the Self through constant meditation on the Self. The mind is refined or purified by meditation. The mind that is rendered pure will naturally move towards the Self. It is not attracted by nor is it attached to the sensual objects.Sankhya Yoga is Jnana Yoga. The aspirant does Vichara (analysis

and unchanging.The Karma Yogi surrenders his actions and their fruits to the Lord. He has Isvarapana Buddhi (intelligence that offers everything to God). This produces purity of mind which gives rise to knowledge of the Self. Karma Yoga brings about concentration of the mind through the purification of the mind. It leads to Yoga through the purification of the mind and so it is spoken of as Yoga itself.Those who practise Sankhya Yoga are the highest class of spiritual aspirants. Those who practise the Yoga of meditation are aspirants of the middling class. Those who practise Karma Yoga are the lowest class of spiritual aspirants. The aspirants of the middling and lowest class soon become aspirants of the highest class through rigorous Sadhana or spiritual practices. (Cf.V.5VI.46)

acts.Commentary These acts Creation and dissolution of the universe. I am the only cause of dissolution of the universe. I am the only cause of Nature and its activities and yet

do nothing. Nor do I cause anything to be done.I remain as one neutral or indifferent or unconcerned. I have no attachment for the fruits of those actions. Further I have not go the egoistic feeling of agency I do this. I know that the Self is actionless. Therefore the actions involved in creation and dissolution do not bind Me.As in the case of Isvara so in the case of others also the absence of the egoistic feeling of agency and the absense of attachment to the fruits of action is the cause of freedom (from Dharma and Adharma

and evil) The ignorant man who works with egoism and who expects rewards for his action is bound by his own actions like the silkworm in the cocoon.Just as the neutral referee or umpire in a cricket or football match is not affected by the victory or defeat of the parties
also the Lord is not affected by the creation and destruction of this world as He remains unconcerned or indifferent and as He is a silent and changeless witness. (Cf.IV.14)

quizOptions.value: Understanding 'Me' as the supreme Spirit helps one attain liberation by providing a clear focus on the eternal, unchanging reality beyond the temporary world governed by the Gunas.
quizOptions.label: Understanding 'Me' as the supreme Spirit helps one attain liberation by providing a clear focus on the eternal, unchanging reality beyond the temporary world governed by the Gunas.

quizOptions.value: For a seer to perceive no agent other than the three Gunas means recognizing that all actions in the material world are driven by these fundamental qualities: sattva, rajas, and tamas.
quizOptions.label: For a seer to perceive no agent other than the three Gunas means recognizing that all actions in the material world are driven by these fundamental qualities: sattva, rajas, and tamas.

quizOptions.value: This understanding helps one attain liberation by focusing on the eternal nature of the Spirit rather than being entangled in the temporary fluctuations of the Gunas.
quizOptions.label: This understanding helps one attain liberation by focusing on the eternal nature of the Spirit rather than being entangled in the temporary fluctuations of the Gunas.

thematic_curriculum.title: Bhagavad Gita: A Thematic Learning Path
thematic_curriculum.description: A lesson-based introduction to the Bhagavad Gita, organized by ideas and supported by chapter and verse references.

sections.title: Arjuna's Grief
sections.subtitle: A crisis becomes a question
sections.description: Meet Arjuna on the battlefield as concern for family, duty, and the consequences of violence overwhelm him. Notice how admitting confusion opens the way to learning.
learning_objectives: Recognize Arjuna's conflict
Explain why he asks Krishna for guidance
Distinguish grief from a considered resolution

questions.prompt: What most directly causes Arjuna to hesitate before the battle?
options: He sees teachers, relatives, and friends among those assembled
He has forgotten how to use his bow
He does not know where the battlefield is
He wants to become king immediately
questions.correct_answer: He sees teachers, relatives, and friends among those assembled
questions.explanation: Arjuna's distress grows as he recognizes loved ones and respected elders on both sides.

questions.prompt: What does Arjuna do after explaining his doubts to Krishna?
options: He asks Krishna to guide him
questions.correct_answer: He asks Krishna to guide him
questions.explanation: His request for instruction marks the shift from argument toward a student seeking counsel.

questions.prompt: Arjuna's first reaction is a calm, detached analysis of his duty.
questions.correct_answer: False
questions.explanation: The opening chapter depicts a deeply personal emotional crisis; reflective instruction follows.

sections.title: The Eternal Soul
sections.subtitle: What changes, and what does not
sections.description: Explore Krishna's teaching that the embodied self is distinct from the changing body, and consider how this view reframes loss and change.
learning_objectives: Summarize the body and self distinction
Interpret the clothing metaphor
Connect impermanence with perspective

questions.prompt: In Krishna's teaching, what changes while the self is described as enduring?
questions.correct_answer: The body
questions.explanation: Krishna compares bodily change to changing garments while describing the self as enduring.

questions.prompt: What does the image of changing clothes illustrate?
options: The embodied self moves on from an old body to a new one
questions.correct_answer: The embodied self moves on from an old body to a new one
questions.explanation: The clothing image in BG2.22 compares the discarded body to worn garments.

questions.prompt: Krishna describes the self as something that weapons can destroy.
questions.correct_answer: False
questions.explanation: BG2.23 says the self is not destroyed by weapons, fire, water, or wind.

sections.title: Act Without Attachment
sections.subtitle: Give your effort; release your grip
sections.description: Learn the Gita's influential teaching on action: attend to the work you can do without making its reward the sole measure of your choices.
learning_objectives: State what is within one's control
Distinguish nonattachment from inaction
Apply the teaching to an everyday task

questions.prompt: According to BG2.47, what is within your control?
options: Your action, not a guaranteed result
questions.correct_answer: Your action, not a guaranteed result
questions.explanation: The verse directs attention to action without claiming ownership over its fruits.

questions.prompt: Nonattachment to results means a person should stop acting altogether.
questions.correct_answer: False
questions.explanation: The teaching calls for responsible action without fixation on reward; it does not praise idleness.

questions.prompt: A student prepares carefully for an exam but cannot control the questions or final score. Which response best reflects BG2.47?
options: Do the preparation sincerely and accept that the score is not fully controllable
Refuse to study because results are uncertain
Study only if a top score is guaranteed
questions.correct_answer: Do the preparation sincerely and accept that the score is not fully controllable
questions.explanation: The practical focus is sincere effort, while recognizing that outcomes depend on more than one's effort alone.

sections.title: The Steady Mind
sections.subtitle: Wisdom in the middle of change
sections.description: Meet the sthitaprajna, the person of steady wisdom, and examine the Gita's account of desire, attention, and inner balance.
learning_objectives: Identify qualities of steady wisdom
Trace how attachment can grow into distress
Choose a pause before reacting

questions.prompt: How does Krishna describe a person of steady wisdom when desires arise?
options: They are not ruled by every desire and remain inwardly composed
questions.correct_answer: They are not ruled by every desire and remain inwardly composed
questions.explanation: BG2.55 describes one who gives up compulsive desires and is content in the self.

questions.prompt: What chain does BG2.62-63 warn can begin with dwelling repeatedly on an object?
questions.correct_answer: Attachment, desire, and eventually confusion
questions.explanation: The verses trace how repeated contemplation can lead through attachment and desire toward anger and loss of discernment.

questions.prompt: Equanimity in BG2.56 means never feeling anything.
questions.correct_answer: False
questions.explanation: The teaching concerns steadiness amid pleasure and pain, rather than emotional numbness.

sections.title: Duty and Selfless Service
sections.subtitle: Work that serves beyond the self
sections.description: See why action is unavoidable and how work performed with care and without selfish attachment can support a wider good.
learning_objectives: Explain why inaction is not the answer
Describe action as service
Reflect on one's responsibilities

questions.prompt: Why does Krishna say that a person cannot remain completely inactive?
options: Everyone is impelled to act by qualities of nature
questions.correct_answer: Everyone is impelled to act by qualities of nature
questions.explanation: BG3.5 notes that no one can remain actionless, even for a moment.

questions.prompt: What distinguishes action performed as yajna in BG3.9?
options: It is offered in a spirit of service rather than selfish attachment
It is done only for praise
questions.correct_answer: It is offered in a spirit of service rather than selfish attachment
questions.explanation: BG3.9 contrasts action tied to sacrifice or service with action that binds through selfish attachment.

questions.prompt: A team member quietly handles an important task that helps the whole group. What best reflects selfless service?
options: Do the task responsibly without making recognition the only goal
Avoid the task unless everyone notices
Take credit for another person's work
questions.correct_answer: Do the task responsibly without making recognition the only goal
questions.explanation: Selfless service values responsible contribution while loosening the demand for personal reward.

sections.title: Knowledge and Renewal
sections.subtitle: Wisdom transforms action
sections.description: Explore the transmission of yoga, Krishna's account of restoring dharma, and the role of knowledge in freeing action from confusion.
learning_objectives: Recognize the teacher and student lineage
Summarize the purpose of divine descent
Connect knowledge with wise action

questions.prompt: Why does Krishna say he appears age after age?
options: To protect the good, restrain harmful forces, and re-establish dharma
questions.correct_answer: To protect the good, restrain harmful forces, and re-establish dharma
questions.explanation: BG4.7-8 describes divine manifestation in relation to dharma and the protection of beings.

questions.prompt: In BG4.34, how is knowledge approached?
options: With humility, inquiry, and service to those who know
questions.correct_answer: With humility, inquiry, and service to those who know
questions.explanation: BG4.34 names respectful approach, sincere questions, and service as ways to learn from the wise.

questions.prompt: BG4.38 presents knowledge as a powerful purifier over time.
questions.correct_answer: True
questions.explanation: Krishna calls knowledge supremely purifying and says it is found in time by one perfected in yoga.

sections.title: Training the Mind
sections.subtitle: Practice and patient return
sections.description: Learn the Gita's practical response to a restless mind: repeated practice, detachment, and patient redirection.
learning_objectives: Describe the mind as both support and obstacle
Name two supports for steadiness
Practice returning attention without self-judgment

questions.prompt: What two supports does Krishna name for mastering the restless mind?
questions.correct_answer: Practice and detachment
questions.explanation: BG6.35 acknowledges the mind is difficult to control but says it can be restrained through practice and detachment.

questions.prompt: When attention wanders during meditation, what does BG6.26 advise?
options: Bring it back and place it again on the self
Follow every thought to its end
questions.correct_answer: Bring it back and place it again on the self
questions.explanation: The practice is to notice wandering and gently return the mind to the intended focus.

questions.prompt: BG6.5 encourages a person to uplift themselves through the mind.
questions.correct_answer: True
questions.explanation: The verse presents the mind as capable of serving as one's friend or one's obstacle.

sections.title: Devotion in Daily Life
sections.subtitle: Offer what you have, with care
sections.description: Study devotion as remembrance, offering, and a way of meeting ordinary actions with sincerity and care.
learning_objectives: Recognize the value of a sincere offering
Identify qualities of a devoted person
Connect remembrance with everyday action

questions.prompt: What does BG9.26 say Krishna accepts when offered with devotion?
options: A leaf, flower, fruit, or water
questions.correct_answer: A leaf, flower, fruit, or water
questions.explanation: The verse emphasizes the loving devotion with which a simple offering is given.

questions.prompt: How does BG9.27 invite a person to approach daily activity?
options: Offer actions, food, and efforts to the divine
Keep daily actions separate from values
questions.correct_answer: Offer actions, food, and efforts to the divine
questions.explanation: The verse extends offering to ordinary actions, eating, giving, and disciplined effort.

questions.prompt: Which quality appears among those dear to Krishna in Chapter 12?
questions.correct_answer: Kindness toward all beings
questions.explanation: Chapter 12 describes the devotee as friendly and compassionate, among other qualities.

sections.title: Seeing the Divine
sections.subtitle: The many and the one
sections.description: Follow Arjuna's request to see Krishna's universal form and reflect on how the Gita presents the divine presence throughout existence.
learning_objectives: Understand why Arjuna asks for a vision
Recognize the universal form as encompassing all existence
Reflect on humility before the vast

questions.prompt: Why does Arjuna ask Krishna to reveal the universal form?
options: He wants to directly witness Krishna's cosmic nature
He wants to end the dialogue
He wants to test his bow
He asks for a map of the battlefield
questions.correct_answer: He wants to directly witness Krishna's cosmic nature
questions.explanation: After hearing Krishna's teachings, Arjuna asks to see the divine form directly, if Krishna considers him able.

questions.prompt: What does Arjuna's vision of the universal form communicate?
options: The divine form encompasses the many dimensions of the cosmos
The universe is limited to one family
questions.correct_answer: The divine form encompasses the many dimensions of the cosmos
questions.explanation: Chapter 11 depicts a form containing countless beings and aspects of the universe.

questions.prompt: Arjuna sees the universal form using only ordinary vision.
questions.correct_answer: False
questions.explanation: Krishna grants Arjuna divine vision to behold the form.

sections.title: Choice and Surrender
sections.subtitle: Understand, reflect, then choose
sections.description: Reach the dialogue's close: Krishna offers instruction, Arjuna reflects, and the learner is invited to act with understanding and resolve.
learning_objectives: Recognize the place of reflection and choice
Summarize the dialogue's resolution
Connect learning with a considered next step

questions.prompt: After teaching Arjuna, what does Krishna invite him to do in BG18.63?
options: Reflect on the teaching and then act as he chooses
questions.correct_answer: Reflect on the teaching and then act as he chooses
questions.explanation: Krishna tells Arjuna to reflect fully on the teaching and then do as he wishes.

questions.prompt: What change does Arjuna express near the end of the Gita?
options: His delusion is gone and he will act according to Krishna's word
He asks to return to sleep
questions.correct_answer: His delusion is gone and he will act according to Krishna's word
questions.explanation: In BG18.73 Arjuna says his delusion has been destroyed and that he will act with resolve.

questions.prompt: The Gita ends with Sanjaya describing the dialogue and its significance.
questions.correct_answer: True
questions.explanation: Sanjaya closes the text by recalling the dialogue between Krishna and Arjuna.
